segments.text: Fewer visitors, more customers, less wasted ad spend.
segments.narration: Fewer visitors, more customers, less wasted ad spend.

Your website conversion rate is the percentage of visitors who do what you want them to do. If 100 people visit your site this week and 3 call you, your conversion rate is 3 percent. Most small business owners obsess over traffic numbers.

If it converts 5 percent or more, you're winning. Take your total conversions in a month. For a roofer, a "conversion" is a phone call or a quote request, not a newsletter signup. For a dentist, it's a booked appointment. For a coffee shop, it might be a reservation or a directions click.

Second, the page doesn't say what you do or where you do it. A visitor lands, scans for two seconds, and either gets the answer or leaves. If your headline says "Excellence In Service Since 1998" instead of "Licensed HVAC Repair In Tucson, Same Day Service," you lose.

Hit that and you'll see calls go up within a month. Your homepage headline is the single most valuable line of text on your website. Most are wasted on slogans nobody cares about. A converting headline answers three questions in one sentence: What do you do?

Every extra field drops your form completion rate. If you sell products, the cart is where the money leaks out. The average online shopping cart abandonment rate is 70.19 percent . Seven out of ten people who add something to their cart leave without buying.

Some buyers want to call before they pay. If you sell services, the same rules apply to your quote request page. The only way to find out is to test. Businesses that A/B tested landing pages before publishing reported a 30 percent average revenue lift compared to those that didn't .

Add your physical address and a Google Map embed on your contact page. Display your license number if your trade requires one. Add three customer quotes with full names and a city. "Mike R., Tempe" reads more honest than "M.R., Customer." If you have video testimonials, even better.

Fix your targeting before you buy more clicks. Pick one fix from this article and ship it before Friday. Small changes compound fast, and the business that tests this month beats the one still talking about it next quarter.
